q: 1. The estimated time required to complete an activity is known as
options: duration
float
restraint
all of these
explain: Duration is the predicted span of time necessary to finish a task, excluding holidays or non-working periods.

q: 2. When float or slack of an activity is positive
options: it represents a situation where extra resources are available and the completion of project is not delayed
it represents that a programme falls behind schedule and additional resources are required to complete the project in time
the activity is critical and any delay in its performance will delay the completion of whole project
any one of the above
explain: Positive float indicates a 'safety margin'. The activity can be delayed by that amount without impacting the project deadline.

options: helps in ascertaining time schedules
makes better and detailed planning possible
provides a standard method for communication project plans, schedules time and cost performance
all of the above
explain: CPM is a comprehensive planning technique used to determine the sequence of critical activities and manage the overall project timeline and resources.

q: 4. Which of the following statement is correct?
options: When float of an activity is zero, it falls only on critical path.
C.P.M. technique is useful to minimise the direct and indirect expenses.
Critical path of a network represents the minimum time required for completion of project.
All of the above
explain: All statements are true: Zero float identifies critical activities, CPM balances costs, and the critical path duration is the fastest the project can finish.

q: 5. When float of an activity is negative
options: it represents a situation where extra resources are available and the completion of project is delayed
it represents that a programme falls behind schedule and additional resources are required to complete the project in time
the activity is critical and any delay in its performance will delay the completion of whole project
all of the above
explain: Negative float occurs when the required completion date is earlier than the calculated earliest finish date, meaning the project is currently behind schedule.

q: 6. Which of the following statement is wrong?
options: an activity consumes time and resources whereas an event do not consume time or resources.
the performance of a specific task is called an activity
an event is an instantaneous point in time at which an activity begins or ends
none of the above
explain: None of the statements are wrong. Options (a), (b), and (c) correctly define the fundamental building blocks of a network diagram.

options: is the head events as well as a tail event
consumes no time
is the beginning of one event and the end of another
is any event other than the initial and final events
explain: A dual role event acts as the end (head) of preceding activities and the start (tail) of succeeding activities. Only the very first and very last events of a project are NOT dual role.

q: 8. In P.E.R.T., the critical path represents the
options: shortest path of the earliest completion of the project
longest path of the network from the initial to final event
ideal path by proceeding along which the project can be completed as per schedule
path which takes into account the completion of the parallel activities
explain: Regardless of CPM or PERT, the critical path is always the sequence of activities that represents the longest duration through the network.

options: the shortest time required to complete the activity under favorable conditions
the maximum time required to complete the activity under adverse conditions
the time the activity would most often require if normal conditions prevail
none of the above
explain: The optimistic time ($t_o$) is the minimum possible time needed to complete an activity if everything goes perfectly.

q: 10. If to, tp and tl represent the optimistic, pessimistic and most likely time estimates, the expected time of completion of the activity is given by
options: te = (to + tl + tp) / 3
te = (to + 2tl + tp) / 4
te = (to + 3tl + tp) / 5
te = (to + 4tl + tp) / 6
explain: The PERT formula for Expected Time is a weighted average that gives 4 times the weight to the most likely time: $t_e = (t_o + 4t_m + t_p) / 6$. (Note: $t_l$ is used here as most likely).
